newsitem.title: USA: FDIC leaves premiums unchanged for banks.
newsitem.headline: FDIC leaves premiums unchanged for banks.

text.p: The healthiest banks will continue to pay no premiums in the first half of 1997 to the fund that insures deposits, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp. decided Tuesday.

The most troubled banks will still pay 27 cents per $100 of insured deposits to the Bank Insurance Fund, an FDIC spokesman said. The range of bank premiums was unchanged from the second half of this year.
The healthiest banks will also be refunded a $500 payment made for the fourth quarter which was eliminated under banking legislation passed in September.
The legislation did away with the minimum $2,000 per year that banks had to contribute to the Bank Insurance Fund regardless of the zero premium, the FDIC spokesman said.
The total amount of the refund to the banking industry will be $4.5 million, he said.

The FDIC also announced the amount that will be required from banks and thrifts for interest payments on Financing Corp. bonds in the first half of 1997. The bonds were issued in the late 1980s to help with the savings and loan cleanup.
Thrifts will have to pay 3.2 cents per $100 of deposits, while banks will be required to pay 0.64 cent per $100 of deposits, the FDIC spokesman said.
